newsitem.title: NORWAY: Greek cargo ship sinks off Norway.
newsitem.headline: Greek cargo ship sinks off Norway.

text.p: A Greek cargo ship sank in a storm off southwestern Norway on Saturday with a crew of 20 Poles, Norwegian rescue officials said.
They said the ship, the Leros Strength, went down about 30 miles west of the Norwegian North Sea port of Stavanger and a helicopter dispatched to the scene saw no survivors.

"There was a Polish crew of 20 people on board," said Elvbjoerg Vaage, spokeswoman for the Stavanger rescue service. "The skipper called at 7.50 a.m. (0650gmt) to say the boat was taking in water from a hole in the bow. While one of us at the rescue centre was speaking to him, the line went dead."
She said the helicopter later searched for an hour for the ship, which went down in waves six metres (20 feet) high.
"There were bubbles on the surface and two empty lift rafts were floating in the sea. There was no trace of the ship or the crew," Vaage told Reuters.

The ship, a 22,000 tonne bulk carrier, was freighting iron ore from Murmansk, Russia, to Poland. The ship was registered on Cyprus but owned by Greek shipping company Leros Management, officials said.
